title: Telnet management enabled
detail: Interface internal allows: ping https ssh http telnet snmp.
recommendation: Remove telnet from allowaccess.

title: Management exposed on internet-facing interface
detail: WAN interface wan1 accepts https, ssh; no trusted hosts on: admin, contractor.
recommendation: Remove management from WAN interfaces; manage over VPN or a dedicated management network. If unavoidable, restrict with local-in policies and trusted hosts.

title: REST API user without trusted hosts
detail: API user 'old-integration' has no trusted hosts.
recommendation: Restrict the API user to the IPs of the systems that use the token.

title: Risky service reachable from the internet
detail: #32 'rdp-to-fileserver': RDP reachable from Any (internet) via 192.168.1.10:3389 (VIP VIP_RDP).
recommendation: Remove the inbound rule, or put the service behind VPN with MFA. If it must stay public, restrict the source to known addresses and apply an IPS profile.

title: Deny rule never applies
detail: Deny #12 'block-bad-host' is shadowed by earlier accept #10 'LAN-internet'.
recommendation: Move this deny rule above the accept rule that shadows it, or narrow the accept rule.

title: Administrator without multi-factor authentication
detail: Admin 'admin' (super_admin) signs in with a password only.
recommendation: Assign FortiToken (or another two-factor method) to every local administrator, or authenticate admins against a RADIUS/SAML server that enforces MFA.

detail: #10 'LAN-internet': all -> any internet destination, all services (internal -> virtual-wan-link).
recommendation: Limit outbound services to what is needed (web, DNS, NTP, mail relays) and apply application control, web and DNS filtering to the rule.

detail: Accept #22 'web-to-db' is shadowed by earlier deny #21 'dmz-deny-lan'.
recommendation: Disable it, or move it above the deny rule if the access is actually needed.

title: SNMP v1/v2c community enabled
detail: Community #1 answers SNMP v1/v2c from any address; SNMP is allowed on internal.
recommendation: Move monitoring to SNMPv3 with auth-priv, limit it to the monitoring servers, and disable the community.

title: SSL-VPN portal open to the whole internet
detail: SSL-VPN listens on wan1 port 10443 for Any (internet). No enabled firewall policy uses ssl.root, so the portal may serve no purpose - consider disabling it.
recommendation: Restrict source addresses (geo or known ranges), enforce MFA, keep firmware patched against FortiGuard PSIRT advisories, and plan migration to IPsec/IKEv2 dial-up, which Fortinet recommends over SSL-VPN tunnel mode.

title: SSL-VPN allows TLS older than 1.2
recommendation: Set ssl-min-proto-ver tls1-2 (or tls1-3).

title: IKEv1 aggressive mode with pre-shared key
detail: Phase 1 'branch-vpn' (site-to-site) uses IKEv1 aggressive mode with a pre-shared key.
recommendation: Move the tunnel to IKEv2 (or at least main mode), and use certificates or a long random PSK.

title: IPsec tunnel allows weak cryptography
recommendation: Use AES-GCM or AES-256 with SHA-256 or better, and DH group 14 or higher (19/20/21 preferred), on both peers.

title: Strong crypto disabled
recommendation: Enable strong-crypto in system global.

recommendation: Remove http from allowaccess.

title: Weak admin lockout
detail: Admins are locked out after 3 failed attempts for 60 seconds (the default).
recommendation: Lock out after 3 failed attempts for at least 15 minutes (CIS: threshold 3, duration 900).

recommendation: Remove management from WAN interfaces; manage over VPN or a dedicated management network. If unavoidable, restrict with local-in policies and trusted hosts.

title: Default 'admin' account exists
recommendation: Create named admin accounts and delete or rename 'admin'.

title: Rule uses an expired schedule
recommendation: Delete the rule (and the schedule) or extend the schedule if the access is still needed.

title: Internet-facing rule without IPS

recommendation: Apply an IPS sensor (and SSL inspection where possible) to every inbound rule.

title: IPS sensor does not block botnet connections

recommendation: Set scan-botnet-connections block on the IPS sensors used by internet-bound rules.

title: No deny rule for known-malicious internet sources
detail: 4 rules publish services to the whole internet (#30, #31, #32, #33) with no deny rule above them for Tor, scanner or malicious-server sources.
recommendation: Add a deny policy from the WAN interfaces with internet-service-src set to the Tor, scanner and malicious-server entries, and move it above the inbound rules.
